subject: general
question: It is observed that a child's heart rate is 135 times per minute. The beat frequency of heart is ____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2.25 Hz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **heart rate** refers to the number of times the heart beats per minute.
 
• The **beat frequency** of the heart is the number of beats per second.
 
• To convert the heart rate from beats per minute to beats per second, we divide by **60**.
 
• In this scenario, the child's heart rate is **135 times per minute**.
 
• Dividing 135 by 60 gives us the beat frequency: **135/60 = 2.25 Hz**.
 
• Therefore, the beat frequency of the heart is **2.25 Hz**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **8100 Hz**__

 __
 
• This value is **incorrect** as it does not correspond to the heart rate conversion process.
 
• Such a high frequency is more typical of **sound waves** or other high-frequency phenomena.
 
 
 
• **1.12 Hz**__
 __
 
• This value is **incorrect** because it is not the result of dividing 135 by 60.
 
• A beat frequency of 1.12 Hz would correspond to a heart rate of **67.2 beats per minute**, which is much lower than 135 beats per minute.
 
 
 
• **135 Hz**__
 
 
• This value is **incorrect** because it mistakenly assumes that the heart rate in beats per minute is the same as the beat frequency in Hz.
 
• 135 Hz would imply an extremely high heart rate of **8100 beats per minute**, which is not physiologically possible.
